manifest.citation: Lessmeier, C.; Kimotho, J. K.; Zimmer, D.; Sextro, W. (2016), Condition Monitoring of Bearing Damage in Electromechanical Drive Systems by Using Motor Current Signals of Electric Motors: A Benchmark Data Set for Data-Driven Classification, European Conference of the Prognostics and Health Management Society; KAt DataCenter, Paderborn University

source_acquisition.acquisition_method: Official HTTP RAR4 byte ranges; exact compressed entries extracted using tar
source_acquisition.selection_policy: One first-encountered recording per bearing and each of two predetermined operating conditions; no labels/features used for record selection

manifest.group_definition: Official physical bearing code; all conditions/records/windows remain in one split
manifest.regime_definition: Known rotational speed / load torque / radial force from official N/M/F setting
manifest.split_strategy: Lexicographic physical-bearing split within damage class, approximately 60/20/20 with at least one bearing per class per split
limitations: Laboratory test rig measurements, not a live factory deployment
Includes accelerated-life and/or artificially damaged bearings; damage method must not be conflated with naturally occurring field failure
Eight windows from each record are correlated, never eight independent bearings
Small subset has one validation bearing per class; no calibrated reliability claim
Noncommercial license; commercial reuse requires provider permission

rac_diagnostics.loss_adapter: classification balanced error; private scalar compatibility only
rac_diagnostics.attention_evidence: physical bearings only; at least five independent groups
